text_blocks.snippet: Replacing a roof in Utah averages roughly [Highlight start] $8,500 to $16,000 [Highlight end] for a typical home, though total costs widely range from $5,200 to $30,000+ depending on roof size, material, and complexity.

list.snippet: Asphalt Shingles: ~$4.50 – $8.25 per sq. ft. (often $8,000 – $16,500 for average-sized homes)
Metal Roofing: ~$8.00 – $17.00 per sq. ft. (popular in mountain and snow-heavy areas because snow sheds easily and resists UV damage)
Designer Shingles / Tile / Specialty: ~$9.00 – $18.00+ per sq. ft. (higher for steep pitches or heavy snow-load framing adjustments)
Roof Size & Pitch: Larger footprints, steeper pitches, and multiple roof planes increase labor and safety costs.
Tear-Off & Decking: Removing multiple existing layers, disposing of debris, and replacing rotted decking add to the base estimate.
Climate & Codes: Heavy snow loads, freeze-thaw cycles, high-altitude UV exposure, and local building permits affect material choices and installation requirements.
Seasonality: Demand often rises from spring through fall, while winter work can face weather delays or snow-removal requirements.

text_blocks.snippet: You can use the IWC Roofing estimator for a quick 60-second personalized roof replacement cost range in Utah. In local discussions, users on Reddit r/SaltLakeCity generally agree that older homes with multiple layers or water damage frequently see quotes in the $12,000 to $21,000 range, while users on Facebook KearnsCommunity share a wide spread of quotes from around $5,000–$10,000 up to $15,000+ or much more for metal roofs.

If you share your approximate home square footage, roofing material (such as asphalt shingles or metal), and any known issues (like steep pitch or multiple shingle layers), I can narrow down a more tailored estimate.
